# A continuous free product system not generated by its tensor core

Alec Kriebel, independent researcher, ORCID [0009-0001-9320-500X](https://orcid.org/0009-0001-9320-500X). Version 1.0, 21 October 2026 UTC. Unrefereed preprint; complete-package clearance and publication remain separate steps.

The paper constructs a continuous separable pointed Hilbert-space free product system E. Its maximal ordered tensor subsystem F is the time-ordered finite-word Fock system. Its closed free hull is precisely the full finite-word sector K, and a nonzero orthogonal grade-omega sector proves K is proper at every positive time. This answers the universal generation question on printed page 530 of Michael Skeide's *Free Product Systems*, [Oberwolfach Reports 6 (2009), 528-530](https://doi.org/10.4171/OWR/2009/09). It makes no separate adapted-cocycle, forward tensor-recovery or general classification claim.

The analytic proof is in `manuscript/main.tex`; the matching PDF is distributed beside this ZIP. The explicit continuity convention, full structural maps and inverses, rational-cut intersection and L2 support-range generation arguments appear in the body. The quantitative grade-omega witness has finite positive measure at least (622/625)(t/3)log(2).
